README: Hover help for every stimgen parameter and GUI control, in one place.
Read through stimgen.util.tooltip(source, key) -- see that function for the
lookup rules. JSON has no comments, hence this key; it is not a section.
Layout: one section per class, named without the package prefix. A lookup
searches the object's own section first, then each superclass section in
turn, so a subclass overrides an inherited entry simply by declaring the
same key (see ClickTrain.Duration). Keys must be valid MATLAB identifiers.
A property whose text depends on another property gets one key per case,
Keep each entry to a single line of plain text: what the parameter does,
plus any non-obvious consequence -- whether it is vectorizable, what a
value of 0 means, which other setting overrides it.

StimType.SoundLevel: Target output level in dB SPL. Only meaningful with a loaded calibration. Enter a vector, e.g. 40:10:80, to make one variant per level.
StimType.ApplyCalibration: Scale the waveform to the calibrated voltage for the requested level. Off: output is normalized only and Sound Level is nominal.
StimType.Duration: Total waveform length in ms. The onset/offset gate is applied inside this duration, not added to it.
StimType.WindowDuration: Combined onset + offset gate length in ms; each ramp is half this value. Ignored when Apply Window is off.
StimType.ApplyWindow: Gate the waveform on and off to suppress the spectral splatter caused by abrupt transitions.
StimType.VariantSelectionMode: Order in which variant combinations are presented: Serial = table order; ShuffleUniform = random; ShuffleLeastUsed = random, favoring the least-presented; CustomSelector = defer to Variant Selector Class.
StimType.VariantCombinationMode: How vector-valued parameters combine: Cartesian = every combination; PairwiseStrict = element-wise, all vectors must be the same length; PairwiseScalarExpand = element-wise with scalars repeated.
StimType.VariantSelectorClass: Class name of a custom variant selector, used only when Variant Selection is CustomSelector. Leave empty otherwise.
StimType.VariantReselectOnUpdate: Pick the next variant every time the signal is regenerated. Off: the active variant stays put until you step it with < / >.

Tone.Frequency: Tone frequency in Hz. Also the key used to look up the calibrated level. Enter a vector, e.g. 2000:1000:8000, to make one variant per frequency.
Tone.OnsetPhase: Starting phase of the carrier in degrees. 0 starts at zero crossing, 90 at the positive peak.
Tone.WindowMethod: Units for Window Duration: Duration = milliseconds; Proportional = percent of Duration; #Periods = carrier periods per ramp. Changing this resets Window Duration.
Tone.WindowDuration_Proportional: Combined onset + offset gate length as a percent of Duration; each ramp is half this value. Ignored when Apply Window is off.
Tone.WindowDuration_Periods: Length of each onset and offset ramp in carrier periods, so the ramp scales with Frequency. Ignored when Apply Window is off.

Noise.HighPass: Lower edge of the noise band in Hz. Must be below Low Pass Fc. Vectorizable.
Noise.LowPass: Upper edge of the noise band in Hz. Must be above High Pass Fc and below Fs/2. Vectorizable.

AMnoise.AMDepth: Modulation depth, 0 = unmodulated noise, 1 = envelope reaches zero (100%). Vectorizable.
AMnoise.AMRate: Sinusoidal modulation frequency in Hz. Vectorizable.
AMnoise.OnsetPhase: Starting phase of the modulator in degrees. The default 180 starts the envelope at its minimum.
AMnoise.EnvelopeOnly: Output the modulation envelope alone, without the noise carrier. Useful for checking the envelope shape.
AMnoise.ApplyViemeisterCorrection: Scale the envelope so that RMS power stays constant as AM Depth changes, keeping depth and level independent.

AttackModNoise.Z: Envelope asymmetry: positive = damped (abrupt onset, gradual decay), negative = ramped (gradual onset, abrupt offset), 0 = symmetric. Larger magnitude = sharper.
AttackModNoise.AMDepth: Modulation depth, 0-1. The envelope shape itself comes from Z; depth here only feeds the Viemeister power correction.
AttackModNoise.AMRate: Repetition rate of the attack envelope in Hz; one envelope per 1/rate seconds. Vectorizable.
AttackModNoise.EnvelopeOnly: Output the modulation envelope alone, without the noise carrier. Useful for checking the envelope shape.
AttackModNoise.ApplyViemeisterCorrection: Scale the envelope so that RMS power stays constant as AM Depth changes, keeping depth and level independent.

FMtone.CarrierFrequency: Center frequency of the carrier in Hz; the modulation sweeps around it. Vectorizable.
FMtone.ModulationFrequency: How fast the frequency sweeps back and forth, in Hz. 0 gives an unmodulated tone at the carrier. Vectorizable.
FMtone.ModulationDepth: Peak frequency deviation in Hz, so the tone spans Carrier +/- this value. 0 gives an unmodulated tone. Vectorizable.
FMtone.OnsetPhase: Starting phase of the carrier in radians (not degrees, unlike Tone and AM Noise).

SweptSine.StartFrequency: Frequency at the start of the sweep, in Hz. Must be below Stop Freq. Scalar only.
SweptSine.StopFrequency: Frequency at the end of the sweep, in Hz. Must be above Start Freq and below Fs/2. Scalar only.
SweptSine.ChirpType: Sweep law: log-sine spends equal time per octave and gives a pink spectrum (preferred for calibration); linear sweeps at a constant Hz/s and emphasizes high frequencies.

ClickTrain.Rate: Clicks per second. The click interval 1/Rate must be at least Click Duration. Vectorizable.
ClickTrain.ClickDuration: Width of a single click in ms; also the key used to look up the calibrated level. Must be at least one sample at the current Fs.
ClickTrain.Polarity: Sign of each click. Alternate flips polarity click by click, which cancels stimulus artifact when responses are averaged.
ClickTrain.OnsetDelay: Silence inserted in ms before the first click. The train shifts later within Train Duration rather than extending it.
ClickTrain.Truncate: Cut the train at Train Duration instead of zero-padding to it, so a train that does not fit a whole number of clicks ends early.
ClickTrain.Duration: Total length of the click train in ms. Clicks that do not fit a whole interval are dropped; the remainder is zero-padded unless Truncate is on.

TORC.LowFrequency: Center frequency for the tonotopic axis, in Hz
TORC.Bandwidth: Frequency range in octaves above the low frequency
TORC.ComponentsPerOctave: Number of component carriers per octave
TORC.ComponentMode: Range: single density across rate scan; Explicit: custom rate/density pairs
TORC.RippleDensity: Ripple spectral density (cycles/octave); sign sets direction of spectral movement
TORC.LowestRate: Lowest temporal modulation rate for Range mode
TORC.HighestRate: Highest temporal modulation rate for Range mode
TORC.ComponentRates: Space-separated list of temporal modulation rates for Explicit mode
TORC.ComponentDensities: Space-separated list of ripple densities for Explicit mode; recycled if shorter than rates
TORC.RandomizeRipplePhase: Randomize ripple phases to reduce spectral peakiness
TORC.Seed: Random seed for carrier and ripple phases; negative value reseeds randomly each update
TORC.ModulationDepth: Peak-to-peak level excursion of the dynamic spectrum
TORC.NumPeriods: Number of ripple periods to include in the stimulus duration

SoundFile.BrowseFiles: Add sound files to this object's catalog. Files are added, not replaced, and each becomes one entry addressable by File Index.
SoundFile.UseAllFiles: Set File Index to every file in the catalog, making one variant per file.
SoundFile.FileIndex: Which catalog entries to play, by position. This is the variant axis: 1:8 makes eight variants. Duration follows the selected file.
SoundFile.Channel: Channel to take from a multichannel file. 0 mixes all channels to mono.
SoundFile.CalibrationMode: Filtered = equalize the whole spectrum with the calibration filter, best for broadband material; Direct = no equalization, level taken at Anchor Freq, preserves the native spectrum; None = normalize only.
SoundFile.AnchorFrequency: Frequency whose calibration value sets the level in Direct mode. 0 uses the waveform's spectral centroid. Ignored in the other modes.
SoundFile.LevelReference: Waveform statistic that Sound Level refers to: rms suits continuous material, peak suits transients with a high crest factor.

StimPlayer.StimTypeDD: Stimulus class that Add Stim will create. The list is every stimulus class found in the stimgen package.
StimPlayer.AddBtn: Add a stimulus of the type above to the bank.
StimPlayer.RemoveBtn: Delete the selected stimulus from the bank.
StimPlayer.BankList: Stimuli in the bank. Select one to edit its parameters, preview it, or step its variants. A run presents every item.
StimPlayer.BankLabel: Name for this bank item, shown in the list and used as its field name when the bank is exported to the workspace.
StimPlayer.Reps: Presentations of the selected bank item per run. Applies to that item only; other items keep their own count.
StimPlayer.ISI: Time between presentations, in ms, for the whole bank. Enter one value for a fixed interval or [min max] to draw each interval uniformly from that range.
StimPlayer.SampleRate: Sample rate used to generate every stimulus in the bank, in Hz. Changing it rebuilds all bank signals at the new rate. When a protocol is running on hardware that reports its own rate, Run adopts that rate instead.
StimPlayer.Order: Order in which bank items are drawn during a run: Shuffle picks at random among items with reps left, Serial works down the list.
StimPlayer.ComboPrevBtn: Show the previous variant combination of the selected stimulus (also the left arrow key).
StimPlayer.ComboNextBtn: Show the next variant combination of the selected stimulus (also the right arrow key).
StimPlayer.ComboStatusLbl: Variant combination now displayed, out of the total produced by this stimulus's vector-valued parameters.
StimPlayer.PlayBtn: Preview the displayed combination of the selected stimulus through the sound card. Preview only: it does not use the hardware or the run counter.
StimPlayer.PlayAllBtn: Preview every variant combination of the selected stimulus in turn. Press again (Stop) to interrupt the cycle.
StimPlayer.RunBtn: Start the session: connect the loaded protocol, reset the counters and present the bank on the internal timer. Press again (Stop) to end it.
StimPlayer.PauseBtn: Hold the run without resetting it; press again (Resume) to carry on from the same counts.
StimPlayer.ProtocolStatusLabel: Loaded protocol and hardware connection state. Without a protocol, or with parameters missing, playback falls back to sound-card preview.
StimPlayer.ComputingLamp: Lit while a stimulus signal is being generated. The GUI is briefly unresponsive during this time.
StimPlayer.StatusLabel: Most recent player action or error.
StimPlayer.Counter: Stimuli presented so far out of the total for this run, summed over the bank (each item contributes its own Reps).

CalibrationGui.MaxOutputVoltage: Output ceiling of the rig, in volts. Sets the clipping limits drawn on the waveform and the line above which a required drive voltage is unreachable.
CalibrationGui.ShowLivePlots: Update the panels during a sweep, measurement by measurement, instead of only when it finishes.
CalibrationGui.SpectrumUnits: Y-axis of the spectrum panel. dB SPL is the calibration's own scale. V rms and dB re 1 V read the microphone signal as the input stage sees it, which is how you tell a quiet room from an overloaded preamp. The per-Hz densities are the comparable way to read a noise floor, since a per-bin level depends on the analysis window. dB re peak shows shape alone -- harmonics and sidebands -- on a rig whose reference has not been measured yet. Applies to the last measurement immediately; nothing is re-acquired.
CalibrationGui.BtnReference: Step 1: Record an acoustic calibrator (e.g. PCB CAL150) held on the microphone to update microphone sensitivity. Records only -- nothing is played through the speaker.
CalibrationGui.BtnBackground: Optional but recommended, after Measure Reference: record the acoustic background with nothing presented and analyze it -- broadband and A-weighted level, fractional-octave band levels, and tonal components such as mains hum. Records only; nothing is played, so take the calibrator off the microphone first and leave the rig as an experiment would find it. The result is plotted on the transfer panel and saved in the .esgc; View > Background Noise Analysis brings it back after another view has taken the panel.
CalibrationGui.BtnTones: Step 2: Run tone frequency sweep to build the tone calibration table by direct measurement.
CalibrationGui.BtnSweptSine: Optional: Broadband calibration with a swept-sine chirp. Can also serve tone lookups -- see Tone Lookup From Swept Sine.
CalibrationGui.ToneLutFromSweptSine: Serve tone lookups (Tone stimuli, filter/noise level anchoring) from the swept sine calibration instead of the direct tone table. While checked this overrides any direct tone calibration; until swept sine data exists the direct tone table still applies. Both tables stay stored, and the choice is saved in the .esgc file.
CalibrationGui.BtnTestTones: Step 3: Verify the tone table -- play discrete tones at the drive voltages the table asks for and compare the levels that come back to the levels requested. Defaults probe midway between the calibrated frequencies, where the table is interpolating, at three levels. Follows Tone Lookup From Swept Sine, so it tests whichever table a Tone stimulus is actually scaled by. Enabled once a tone or swept sine calibration exists and hardware is attached.
CalibrationGui.BtnFilter: Step 4 (optional): Design equalization filter after tone or swept sine calibration. Prompts for filter length, design method, interpolation, smoothing, correction limit and band, then opens the result in fvtool.
CalibrationGui.BtnTestFilter: Step 5 (optional): Verify the designed filter empirically -- play the sweep raw and again through the filter, measure both responses, and report how flat the equalized response came out. Enabled once a filter is designed or loaded and hardware is attached.
CalibrationGui.BtnStop: Interrupt a running tone, click, swept-sine calibration, tone table test, or filter test. Takes effect at the next measurement, not instantly; partial calibration data is discarded.
CalibrationGui.BtnReset: Discard all acquired tone/click/swept-sine calibration data and any designed filter, to start over. Keeps the attached adapter, loaded protocol, mic sensitivity, and other settings.

StimInspector.ExportTool: Export Signal and Metrics to Workspace
